Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: How would you react if a stranger approaches you and says you are beautiful?
Answer: Years ago, I was at Pondicherry. With my ex-husband, a friend and his wife. I was wearing my favourite dress. It was new year's eve. All the pubs were crowded and we were looking for a table. Finally, we reached a restaurant with a sea view. This too was crowded and while the husband was talking to the restaurant manager to manage a table for us, I found two old men in their 70s staring at me affectionately. They were foreigners. They looked super lively and cute. When we had eye contact, one of them complimented me by saying, “You are beautiful" and smiled. I blushed purple and thanked him. While my husband had unnerved me by paying more heed to the friend and his wife, these cute-looking old men boosted my confidence for the rest of the evening. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the biggest tragedy in life?
Answer: He was emotional. He was an introvert. He did everything for his children that a father is supposed to do. He loved his wife just the way a husband is supposed to love. Still, no one could reciprocate the same love to him. His children considered him a burden as he was reaching retirement. His wife has always been least bothered about him as she was influenced by modern thoughts and so-called freedom. He wondered if he could ever speak up against the misbehaviour that he received from his family. He wondered if he could ever know his fault for this mistreatment. He kept quiet as he felt emotional and helpless. He lived in silence as he didn't learn to raise his voice. He endured the pain of negligence and lived like an anonymous in his own house. He could never share this emotional turmoil with anyone outside as the fear of being judged and mocked has engulfed him. The belief “A real man is the one who knows to rule" established by society has only encouraged the lions to survive. “Men too can be vulnerable" is not acceptable here. So he lived all his life in negligence and with the feeling of being unwanted. And slowly, he too forgot if he existed. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is the one story your parents always tell about you?
Answer: I was a crybaby. I had the stamina to cry at a stretch for hours. Without taking a break. I could cry the whole night. I woke up and cried when the cradle stopped moving. So my mother had to tie one end of the string in her leg, which was attached to the cradle. She moved her feet to move the cradle during her sleep. The moment the cradle stopped, I cried. People could easily irritate me and watch a cry show and giggle. While crying, I should not be left alone. If I didn't get the attention, I banged my head on the floor or against the wall. So my head was always swollen. If one part was swollen, I made sure I banged it with another part. My mom kept a homeopathy medicine (Arnica) handy for this hurt. So I was a horribly unique child. And Mom was pissed off with me. She wanted to drop me in a bin or at a temple forever. However, my dad still adored me. I think my mother could never succeed in her plans because of him only. I hope you enjoyed the story. A true story that I am also unable to believe. And looking at this innocent face, I feel all the allegations are false. P.S.- Joking apart, my mother had numerous sleepless nights while bringing me up. Her health drastically deteriorated from then and there. I am indebted to her. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.

Name: Anshu Bharti
Question: What is something you have tried, but will never do again?
Answer: Smoking. I would be 10–11 years old. I desperately wanted to smoke. I wanted to experience the puff coming out of the mouth. I was born in a family where tea, coffee, drinks, and smoking were prohibited. My father, being a doctor, has never touched any of these. Talking about them was a crime in my family. However, I had made up my mind to try it. Unfortunately, I could not get cigarettes from any shop as everyone knew my father. The domestic help, who smoked 3–4 bidis in a day, refused to give me one. The poor creature was afraid of my parents. So I invented a Bidi on my own. I managed to get some dry leaves. I crushed them and rolled them on paper. Then I tied it with a thread just like a Bidi is tied up. It was a summer afternoon. When everyone went for a nap, I went backside verandah and smoked my self-made Bidi. As soon as I inhaled it, I got a severe cough that seemed to suffocate me to death. My eyes filled with tears. My face reddened. And out of nowhere, my uncle turned up to give me a slap across my cheek. Tears rolled down. His contribution to reddening my already reddened face was remarkable. He threw the Bidi and warned me not to repeat this. That was the first and last time when I tried smoking. Now, I can't even stand near a smoker. The smell of cigarettes gives me nausea, and I start coughing. Thank you for reading. Stay Calm! Anshu.
